general_information.Syllabus Name: Crisis Communications Management_Quản trị truyền thông khủng hoảng
general_information.Description: This course covers crisis communication theory, crisis management approaches, classic cases and the influence of culture on crisis communication. This course will introduce the definitions of crisis and how they come about, the importance of the Enterprise Risk Management framework in crisis prevention and preparation, and how we can recognise and address crises in case they happen. This course focuses on the role of communications throughout the crisis management process, as well as how to utilise media relations and social media to prevent and/or respond to crises.
general_information.StudentTasks: - Attend more than 80% of contact hours in order to be accepted to the final examination - Actively participate in class activities - Fulfill tasks given by instructor after class - Use their own laptop in class only for learning purpose - Read the textbook in advance - Access the course website (https://flm.fpt.edu.vn/) for up-to-date information and material of the course.

learning_outcomes.CLO Details: Identify organisational, industrial and environmental challenges and disasters
Demonstrate an understanding of the concepts, theories and practice of issues management and crisis communication.
Analyse and develop strategies for organisational issues using the theories, models and methods of issues management and crisis communication
Gain the capacity to critique organisational and industrial responses to issues and crises In terms of attitude and ethics
Develop a critical attitude towards crisis communications management
Identify and apply ethical standards of practice when dealing with issues management and crisis communication
Skills in analysis and problem solving; Proficient in presentation and teamwork skills

assessments.Grading Guide: Option 1: Individual Essay Type: Essay Weight: 20% Length: 3,000 words Task Description: Choose from the list of crisis case studies provided by the lecturer before and analyse one organisational crisis. Your essay will include an overview of the crisis, a description of the organisation, a crisis timeline, actions and responses taken, a media analysis, stakeholder impacts, lessons learned, recommendations, and use appropriate matrix/models. The essay should address the criteria as outlined in the assessment task and rubric mentioned during the class. Studens should use a mix of scholarly references, media coverage and organisational materials. Option 2: (For Constructivism Approach only): Follow lecturer's proposal

assessments.Grading Guide: Option 1: Presentation + Report Crisis Management Plan (In the class) Type: Crisis Group Project Weight: 35% Including: Presentation (15%) + Report (20%) Task Description: Students working within a small group setting of maximum 4 students should select one crisis accepted by the lecturer. Each team will be asked to complete a crisis management plan to address this crisis. The plan must showcase all knowledge the students have gained in the class, including: the three-stage approach, the proactive management functions and the crisis communication system. Students will deliver a final report with their plan to their “organisation” and deliver a 30-minute presentation on its highlights to their “partners” as well as their "organisation's representatives". The crisis communication plan should contain sections which include: 1. Organizational history 2. Risk assessment 3. Strategic communication action plan 4. Evaluation 5. Crisis appendix Notes: Further details of the crisis communication plan will be provided in class. The detailed marking criteria for this assessment will be provided to you by your lecturer. Option 2: (For Constructivism Approach only): Follow lecturer's proposal

assessments.Grading Guide: Option 1: Presentation Media Conference (In the class) Type: Media Conference Weight: 20% Length: 20 mins + 5-15 mins Q&A Task Description: Students work in groups of 3 or 4, develop a media conference based on the scenario your group has been allocated during the class. Your group will have to prepare for a media conference based on the scenario which will respond to a simulated crisis. Your media conference should be no more than 30 minutes in total and will be followed by a 5-15 minute Q&A from the “journalist” members of the class. The conference should include: 1. a media alert 2. at least one media statement (to be delivered at the conference) 3. a one-page summary of key messages The lecturer, through class discussion, is expected to answer student's questions about this assessment. assessments.Grading Guide: Option 1: Report Individual Report (At home) Type: Report Weight: 15% Length: 2,000 words Task Description: For this assignment, you will choose an organisation and identify some of its key issues and stakeholder groups. You will investigate how the issues may impact, or have the potential to impact, on the organisation’s relationship management and public image. For this, you will need to examine a range of sources including organisational documents (e.g. annual reports, website), media (e.g. news coverage and social media platforms) and academic literature (e.g. journal articles and books). Based on your research you will write a 2000-word report which includes key recommendations for the organisation that you have analysed. The lecturer, through class discussion, is expected to answer student's questions about what they are not sure. The lecturer will summarise the key points and emphasize what students have to keep in mind while writng this report. Option 2: (For Constructivism Approach only): Follow lecturer's proposal
